notes: Source wording kept; the first-person setup stays with the narrator. Grandpa walks in with his cane and the hipster gets a beard and round glasses so 'hip' reads on screen.
title: Hip Replacement

lines.text: My grandpa just walked into my room with a young guy wearing skinny jeans and eating avocado toast.
Who is this guy?
This is my hip replacement.

notes: Source wording kept; the student is a schoolboy (vovochka as a child, named David as in the source), the principal is the boss with glasses. The punchline is split in two; 'asshole' softened to 'jerk' in text.
title: David

lines.text: A student visits the principal's office one day.
What's your name, son?
D-d-d-dav-dav-david, sir.
Oh, do you have a stutter?
No sir, my dad has a stutter,
but the guy who registered my name was a jerk.
lines.uncensored: but the guy who registered my name was an asshole.

notes: Translated line by line; 'sir' dropped where it sounds unnatural in Russian, 'asshole' kept as 'мудак' in uncensored, 'козёл' in text.
title: Давид

lines.text: Однажды ученик приходит в кабинет директора.
Как тебя зовут, сынок?
Д-д-д-дав-дав-Давид.
О, ты заикаешься?
Нет, это мой папа заикается,
а вот тот, кто записывал моё имя, был козлом.
lines.uncensored: а вот тот, кто записывал моё имя, был мудаком.

notes: Translated line by line; 'sir' becomes 'Herr Direktor', 'asshole' is 'Arschloch' in uncensored and 'Blödmann' in text.
title: David

lines.text: Eines Tages kommt ein Schüler ins Büro des Direktors.
Wie heißt du, mein Junge?
D-d-d-Dav-Dav-David, Herr Direktor.
Oh, stotterst du?
Nein, Herr Direktor, mein Vater stottert,
aber der Typ, der meinen Namen eingetragen hat, war ein Blödmann.
lines.uncensored: aber der Typ, der meinen Namen eingetragen hat, war ein Arschloch.

notes: Source wording kept; the trouser trick stays with the narrator (we cannot draw it), the woman waits by the car on the highway backdrop and the soldier walks over to the car door.
title: Khakis

lines.text: Finding a woman sobbing that she had locked her keys in her car, a passing soldier assures her that he can help.
She looks on amazed as he removes his trousers, rolls them into a tight ball and rubs them against the car door.
Magically it opens.
That's so clever. How did you do it?
Easy. These are my khakis.

notes: Source wording kept, each long line split in two; the wife wears an apron. The devil is only mentioned, so he stays off screen.
title: Relatives

lines.text: I should've married the devil!
He would've made a better husband than you!
You would've been arrested,
because marriage between relatives is illegal in this country.

notes: Translated line by line; 'relatives' kept as the punch word near the end.
title: Родственники

lines.text: Надо было мне выйти замуж за чёрта!
Он был бы мужем получше тебя!
Тебя бы арестовали,
потому что браки между родственниками в нашей стране запрещены.

notes: Translated line by line; no pun to rebuild.
title: Verwandtschaft

lines.text: Ich hätte den Teufel heiraten sollen!
Der wäre ein besserer Ehemann gewesen als du!
Dann hätte man dich verhaftet,
weil die Ehe zwischen Verwandten hierzulande verboten ist.

notes: Source wording kept, typos fixed (There's, Everything's); the first-person setup stays with the narrator. The wife lies at the bed, the husband sits beside her.
title: Confession

lines.text: My wife was dying. I was by her bedside.
There's something I must confess.
Shhh. There's nothing to confess. Everything's alright.
No, I must die in peace.
I had sex with your brother, your best friend, his best friend and your father.
I know. That's why I poisoned you.

notes: Translated line by line; first-person setup stays with the narrator, punch word 'отравил' last.
title: Исповедь

lines.text: Моя жена умирала. Я сидел у её постели.
Я должна тебе кое в чём признаться.
Тсс. Не в чем признаваться. Всё хорошо.
Нет, я должна умереть спокойно.
Я спала с твоим братом, твоим лучшим другом, его лучшим другом и твоим отцом.
Я знаю. Поэтому я тебя и отравил.

notes: Translated line by line; first-person setup stays with the narrator, punch word 'vergiftet' last.
title: Die Beichte

lines.text: Meine Frau lag im Sterben. Ich saß an ihrem Bett.
Ich muss dir etwas gestehen.
Pssst. Es gibt nichts zu gestehen. Alles ist gut.
Nein, ich muss in Frieden sterben.
Ich hatte Sex mit deinem Bruder, deinem besten Freund, seinem besten Freund und deinem Vater.
Ich weiß. Deshalb habe ich dich vergiftet.

notes: Source wording kept; the answer is split at the semicolon, 'shit' softened to 'crap' in text. The mime is only mentioned, so he stays off screen.
title: Invisible

lines.text: If you became invisible, what would you do first?
I'd go to Paris, find a performing street mime and beat the crap out of him;
lines.uncensored: I'd go to Paris, find a performing street mime and beat the shit out of him;

lines.text: the round of applause he'd get would be astounding.

notes: Translated line by line; 'beat the shit out of him' is 'выбил бы всё дерьмо' in uncensored and 'всю дурь' in text.
title: Невидимка

lines.text: Если бы ты стал невидимым, что бы ты сделал первым делом?
Я бы поехал в Париж, нашёл уличного мима во время выступления и выбил бы из него всю дурь.
lines.uncensored: Я бы поехал в Париж, нашёл уличного мима во время выступления и выбил бы из него всё дерьмо.

lines.text: Аплодисменты ему были бы просто оглушительные.

notes: Translated line by line; 'beat the shit out of him' rendered with the natural idiom 'die Seele aus dem Leib prügeln', which needs no softening, so no uncensored line.
title: Unsichtbar

lines.text: Wenn du unsichtbar wärst, was würdest du als Erstes tun?
Ich würde nach Paris fahren, mir einen Straßenpantomimen mitten in der Vorstellung suchen und ihm die Seele aus dem Leib prügeln.
Der Applaus, den er dafür bekäme, wäre einfach überwältigend.

notes: Source wording kept; the church setting is shown, so no narrator. A few churchgoers murmur after her question, which pays off the punchline that it was not silent.
title: Silent

lines.text: I've let out one of those silent farts.
What do I do?
Change the battery in your hearing aid.

notes: Translated line by line; churchgoers murmur before the punchline, as in the English version.
title: Беззвучно

lines.text: Я только что беззвучно пукнула.
Что мне делать?
Поменяй батарейку в слуховом аппарате.

notes: Translated line by line; churchgoers murmur before the punchline, as in the English version.
title: Lautlos

lines.text: Ich habe gerade einen von diesen lautlosen Pupsern losgelassen.
Was soll ich tun?
Wechsel die Batterie in deinem Hörgerät.

notes: Source wording kept; the answer split in two. The wife sits on the sofa, the husband holds a lottery ticket.
title: The Lottery

lines.text: If you won the lottery, would you still love me?
Of course I would.
I'd miss you, but I'd still love you.

notes: Translated line by line; the husband holds a lottery ticket.
title: Лотерея

lines.text: Если бы ты выиграл в лотерею, ты бы меня всё ещё любил?
Конечно, любил бы.
Я бы по тебе скучал, но всё равно любил бы.

notes: Translated line by line; lottery becomes Lotto, the husband holds the ticket.
title: Der Lottogewinn

lines.text: Wenn du im Lotto gewinnen würdest, würdest du mich dann immer noch lieben?
Natürlich würde ich das.
Ich würde dich vermissen, aber ich würde dich immer noch lieben.
